rationale: The first reply treated 'NN-H98' as the model ('On your Panasonic NN-H98') instead of asking whether H98 was a display code. It also referred to a 'one-minute test' the customer was never asked to run. The second reply correctly read H98 as a high-voltage/no-output fault, kept to the safety boundary and escalated to an engineer or Panasonic without naming a part. It did not mention the working grill/convection modes, a one-time power reset, or the repair-versus-replace cost, though the customer had said they would pay for a sensible repair, so it was a bit thin but safe and appropriate.
